passages.provision_quote: A person whose exercise of religion has been substantially burdened, or is likely to be substantially burdened, by a violation of this chapter may assert the violation or impending violation as a claim or defense in a judicial or administrative proceeding, regardless of whether the state or any other governmental entity is a party to the proceeding.
passages.note: The enrolled act prints the operative chapter but names no voter or sponsor.

rows.reasoning: Wesco sponsored SB 101 (2015) in the House ("Sponsored by: Rep. Timothy Wesco") and voted Yea on its third reading ("Yea 63 Nay 31 Excused 5 Not Voting 0"), a single-subject bill whose enrolled text bars a governmental entity from substantially burdening a person's exercise of religion "even if the burden results from a rule of general applicability" and lets the burdened person "assert the violation or impending violation as a claim or defense in a judicial or administrative proceeding". That is a law that allows "faith-based exemptions from laws that conflict with sincere religious beliefs". It is not "complete autonomy in their operations and hiring practices": the chapter yields whenever the entity shows the burden "is in furtherance of a compelling governmental interest", and Section 11 bars any claim "against any private employer".
